meta.notice: OCO-2 paused science observations 28 Jul–13 Aug 2026 (safe mode); those days stay missing. This release uses OCO-2 data up to 31 Oct 2026 (the data for 1–31 Oct 2026 are preliminary forward-processing data), so monthly values run to September 2026. August–September 2026 are early estimates: dashed on the charts and still revised as data arrive.

products.oco2: OCO-2 Lite 10-s XCO₂: v11.2r (doi:10.5067/70K2B2W8MNGY) through 2023-12-31 and v11.3r (doi:10.5067/C4OENLFCYVSA) from 2024-01-01, through 2026-09-30; then preliminary forward-processing (FP) data from the OCO-2 team (product FwDaily_B11301_r01), 2026-10-01 through 2026-10-31. Method GRESO 1.x (baseline 2026-01-12, 16-day bins dated at their effective time, seasonal fit solved exactly) (Pandey et al. 2024).
products.gosat: ACOS GOSAT v11 Lite soundings (NASA GES DISC, doi:10.5067/UAY6VJYTS8OD), filtered subset acosGOSATv11_lite_20090418-20261031_filtered_tiny.h5, 2009-04-18 → 2026-10-31; same GRESO chain as OCO-2. On the main page, the annual chart and table open with GOSAT on (GOSAT alone for 2010–2014, the mean of OCO-2 and GOSAT from 2015); on the monthly chart it is off until switched on. Uncertainty = smoothing spread + 0.08 ppm/yr floor (no retrieval term). Same status rule as OCO-2.
products.noaa: NOAA GML global marine boundary layer (MBL); Lan, X., Tans, P. and Thoning, K.W., Trends in globally-averaged CO2 determined from NOAA GML measurements, doi:10.15138/9N0H-ZH07. Annual: co2_gr_gl.txt (file created 2026-10-09). Monthly ‘derived from NOAA trend’ is our derivative, not a NOAA product: 12 × the change of the co2_mm_gl.txt trend column (file created 2026-10-09) from the 1st of each month to the 1st of the next (the trend linearly interpolated to 00:00 UTC on those days, as for the annual and 12-month values), then the same 5-month running mean as the OCO-2 values (last two months unsmoothed). It covers the same dates as the OCO-2 monthly values and ends with June 2026, because NOAA’s trend ends in mid-July 2026. Redistributed with this citation and file date; NOAA revises its values, so take the current files from https://gml.noaa.gov/ccgg/trends/global.html for new work.
products.emissions: Friedlingstein et al. (2026), Global Carbon Budget 2025, Earth Syst. Sci. Data 18, 3211-3288, doi:10.5194/essd-18-3211-2026; data doi:10.18160/GCP-2025 (CC BY 4.0): fossil CO₂ excluding the cement-carbonation sink, plus land-use change, through 2024. 2025 onward: low-latency estimate = Carbon Monitor, carbonmonitor.org (Liu et al. 2020, arXiv:2004.13614) × 1.020 (mean GCB/Carbon Monitor ratio 2022–24) plus linearly extrapolated land-use change (provisional; not a budget number). Monthly series: each GCB year spread over the months with Carbon Monitor's monthly pattern (2015–2018 its average pattern, 2019–2024 that year's Carbon Monitor months scaled to the GCB total), land-use change flat within each year, then a fixed seasonal cycle removed. August–September 2026: the same months a year earlier times Carbon Monitor's growth over the year, from Carbon Monitor's data of 10 November 2026 (its newer files have a different seasonal shape, so their monthly values are not joined on directly).
products.oni: NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ERSST.v5), oni.ascii.txt through ASO 2026; date = centre month of the 3-month season.

status_rules.note: Each monthly value gets a status from its age: the number of whole months between the end of that month and the data end (31 Oct 2026). Age 0–2 = early estimate (dashed; revised most as data arrive); 3–5 = provisional (still revised; about 0.7 ppm/yr RMS at 3 months, falling to 0.24 ppm/yr at 5 [revision sizes from an earlier pipeline run; recompute on this release]); 6 or more = final. In this release April 2026 and earlier are final, May–July 2026 provisional and August–September 2026 early. A calendar-year value is provisional until data through the end of February of the following year are in (normally released about April), then final. No partial-year annual values are published. The same rule applies to every chart and file.

gaps.label: OCO-2 safe mode: no data. The 16-day trend is linearly interpolated across the gap, so the Aug and Sep 2017 monthly values rest on the interpolation (flagged in the downloads)

OCO-2 paused science observations 28 Jul–13 Aug 2026 (safe mode after an instrument anomaly); those days stay missing. The 16-day trend is interpolated across the gap, so the Aug 2026 monthly value rests partly on the interpolation (flagged in the downloads). This release uses OCO-2 data up to 30 Sep 2026 from the retrospective stream, which NASA expects to be of nominal quality after the gap (forward-stream data were of reduced quality until 17 Sep 2026), then preliminary forward-processing data for 1–31 Oct 2026

meta.provenance: OCO-2 Lite v11.2r through 2023, v11.3r from 2024.
known_issues: The v11.2r → v11.3r splice falls on 1 Jan 2024, the anchor shared by the 2023 and 2024 annual values.
‘All’ includes snapshot-area-map (SAM) soundings, so it is not exactly land ∪ ocean.
GOSAT uncertainty has no retrieval term (smoothing + 0.08 ppm/yr floor only); GOSAT is not fully independent of OCO-2 (shared ACOS algorithm heritage).
Monthly values carry a larger, unquantified error (order 0.7 ppm/yr); the newest months are revised.
Aug and Sep 2017 and Aug 2026 monthly values rest on the trend interpolated across OCO-2's data gaps (flagged in the monthly and latitude-band files).
GOSAT's 10° band values for January 2015 and January 2026, months without any GOSAT data, come from the interpolation across GOSAT's data gaps alone (flagged in the latitude-band file).
Since 2024 the OCO-2 − GOSAT trend difference oscillates seasonally (0.1–0.17 ppm); do not over-read month-to-month differences between the sensors.
Latitude-band values are the rate of change of XCO₂ over a band, not regional fluxes. The 10° bands come from a separate, closely related run of the method.
The 2025–26 slowdown is not falling emissions: fossil emissions were flat or up about 1%.
The 10° bands use complete 16-day windows only, so they use OCO-2 data to 20 Oct 2026 and GOSAT data to 25 Oct 2026, 11 and 6 days less than the global series.

The OCO-2 data for 1–31 Oct 2026 are preliminary forward-processing (FP) data from the OCO-2 team (product FwDaily_B11301_r01; no data on 6 Oct 2026), used before the public retrospective data for that period are released. The monthly values for Jun–Sep 2026 rest on them (flag preliminary_fp_data) and may change when the public data are used.
meta.method_summary: GRESO (Pandey et al. 2024, doi:10.1029/2023AV001145), method version GRESO 1.x (baseline 2026-01-12, 16-day bins dated at their effective time, seasonal fit solved exactly). Input: OCO-2 v11 10-s XCO₂ (v11.2r through 2023, v11.3r from 2024, preliminary forward-processing data for 1–31 Oct 2026), land + ocean (target mode excluded), retrieval uncertainty < 2 ppm. Each 16-day repeat cycle is binned to 5°×5° cells (median), averaged along each latitude row and area-weighted across rows. Each 16-day bin is dated at its effective time, the area-weighted mean time of the soundings it uses (the same weights as the XCO₂ mean), not at the window's midpoint. Seasonal cycle: least-squares fit (solved exactly) of a cubic polynomial plus four annual harmonics over the whole record; the harmonics are subtracted. The deseasonalized series is gap-filled linearly and smoothed with a 7-window (7×16-day ≈ 112-day) running mean. Monthly growth = trend(1st of next month) − trend(1st of month), ×12 for ppm/yr, displayed with a 5-month running mean. Annual growth = trend(1 Jan Y+1) − trend(1 Jan Y), not the mean of the displayed monthly values. Annual 1σ = √(retrieval² + smoothing² + 0.04²): retrieval = spread over 40 decile subsets of four retrieval parameters, smoothing = spread over 6 smoothing widths, 0.04 ppm/yr = OSSE sampling error.

kpis.summary: Over the 12 months through September 2026, CO₂ built up in the whole atmosphere at 2.4 ppm a year (an early estimate: the newest months are still revised), about 5.1 billion tonnes of carbon: 69% of the 2024 pace, while fossil emissions were flat or up about 1%.

last12.method: Change of the deseasonalized OCO-2 XCO₂ trend between 00:00 UTC on 2025-10-01 and 2026-10-01: the same definition as the annual value (1 Jan → 1 Jan), shifted so that the window ends with September 2026, the newest month with observations (August–September 2026 are early estimates, so the value will still be revised). The trend is used as published (it is already smoothed and is not smoothed again). No NOAA value for these dates: its monthly trend (co2_mm_gl.txt, file created 2026-10-09) ends in mid-July 2026, before the window ends.

latest_month.note: Newest month that is not an early estimate. Months this recent are still revised as data arrive (see the status rule), so it is shown in the chart, not as a headline number.
